repair_checks.evidence: The lesson now states D=alpha-2beta+gamma=2a=y''(r), the fitted parabola's signed curvature. It no longer calls D twice the curvature, and the derivation agrees.

The phase study explicitly freezes N0=64 and fs/N0=16 Hz as the reference-bin unit. The N=256 passage separately identifies the 4 Hz current-record bin and correctly translates 0.05 reference bin to 0.8 Hz or 0.2 current-record bin.

Both the exposition and strategy solution limit the factor-two real-cosine calibration to an interior positive-frequency line whose positive- and negative-frequency window lobes pass the same isolation check.
The estimator is consistently described as producing analytic-tone amplitude magnitude, not a complex amplitude phasor; A-hat=10^(b-hat/20) is unchanged and correct.

A padded-grid step is N/L current-record bins when a current-record bin is fs/N.
At common L=1024, N=256 gives 250 ms, 1 Hz grid spacing, and periodic-Hann width 16 Hz, one quarter of the N=64 width.
alpha, beta, and gamma use 20log10 amplitude magnitudes normalized by Cw; p, fitted height, f-hat, and A-hat match Smith section 5.6.1 after translating FFT size to L.

Q=1 rectangular/Hann/Blackman errors and the Q=4 <0.002 bound exactly match peak-study.mjs; centered and half-bin estimates are symmetry-exact.

Gaussian log magnitude is quadratic only before practical truncation; practical windows are locally quadratic; dense noiseless sampling can drive interpolation error toward zero without changing resolution.

Bin-center p=0, half-bin tied +/-1/2 centers, zero-amplitude nonidentifiability, and coincident-tone phasor-sum boundaries are correct.
The full parabola derivation has correct signs, a=(alpha-2beta+gamma)/2, p formula, b formula, and zero/positive-curvature diagnoses.

Independent execution gives mean 0.021767895758180437, sample SD 0.024899643497250934, and CV 1.1438700264766555, matching every reported digit.
N=64, periodic Hann, Cw=32, L=1024, and k=160 are fixed; k is interior and maps to 160 Hz. Padding does not average realizations.
The standard one-sided factor is 2/Cw for a separated interior real-cosine line and is omitted at DC and even-L Nyquist; both occurrences now include image-isolation.
The reporting ledger correctly separates N, L, window convention, raw-forward scale, coherent response, analytic/real convention, and resolution evidence.
